Name: BackupDrill - Backup Supabase Database
Description:
Backs up a Supabase Postgres database to your own S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 and others) with the open-source [BackupDrill](https://backupdrill.com) CLI. Put it before the step that runs your database migrations, so every deployment has a fresh snapshot with a checksummed `manifest.json` to go back to.

If **Run Restore Drill** is ticked, the step then restores that snapshot into a throwaway Postgres container and checks it: the dump's checksum, that `pg_restore` completes, that every table comes back and that tables which had rows are not empty. If the drill does not pass, the step fails and the deployment stops before anything else runs.

Sets the output variable `SnapshotName` (the folder in the bucket that holds this backup).

**Requirements on the worker:**
- Node.js 20 or later. The CLI runs through `npx`, so nothing is installed globally.
- `pg_dump` with a major version at least that of your Supabase Postgres (15, 16 or 17). The CLI refuses to run an older one.
- For the restore drill: Docker and `pg_restore`.

The database connection string and bucket keys are passed to the CLI as environment variables, not on the command line. By default only the `public` schema is backed up.

Properties.Octopus.Action.Script.ScriptBody:
#!/bin/bash

# BackupDrill - Backup Supabase Database
# Backs up a Supabase Postgres database to your own S3-compatible bucket with the
# open-source backupdrill CLI (npm package "backupdrill"). Optionally restores the new
# snapshot into a throwaway Postgres container and fails the step if that restore drill fails.

DatabaseUrl=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.DatabaseUrl")
S3Bucket=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.S3Bucket")
S3AccessKeyId=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.S3AccessKeyId")
S3SecretAccessKey=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.S3SecretAccessKey")
S3Endpoint=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.S3Endpoint")
S3Region=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.S3Region")
ProjectName=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.ProjectName")
Schemas=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.Schemas")
RunDrill=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.RunDrill")
PgBinDirectory=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.PgBinDirectory")
CliVersion=$(get_octopusvariable "BackupDrill.CliVersion")

fail() {
  echo "ERROR: $1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Exports a setting for the CLI, or removes it when the parameter is blank, so a value
# left in the worker's environment by something else can't change where the backup goes.
export_or_unset() {
  if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
    export "$1=$2"
  else
    unset "$1"
  fi
}

# Validate parameters

if [[ -z "$DatabaseUrl" ]]; then
  fail "Database Connection String (BackupDrill.DatabaseUrl) is required."
fi

case "$DatabaseUrl" in
  postgres://* | postgresql://*) ;;
  *) fail "Database Connection String must start with postgresql:// (use the Session pooler connection string from the Supabase dashboard)." ;;
esac

if [[ -z "$S3Bucket" ]]; then
  fail "Bucket (BackupDrill.S3Bucket) is required."
fi

if [[ -z "$S3AccessKeyId" || -z "$S3SecretAccessKey" ]]; then
  fail "Bucket Access Key ID (BackupDrill.S3AccessKeyId) and Bucket Secret Access Key (BackupDrill.S3SecretAccessKey) are both required."
fi

RunDrill=$(echo "${RunDrill:-False}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
if [[ "$RunDrill" != "true" && "$RunDrill" != "false" ]]; then
  fail "Run Restore Drill (BackupDrill.RunDrill) must be True or False."
fi

CliVersion="${CliVersion:-2}"

# Check tools before downloading anything, so a missing tool fails in seconds

if [[ -n "$PgBinDirectory" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -d "$PgBinDirectory" ]]; then
    fail "PostgreSQL Client Directory '$PgBinDirectory' does not exist on this worker."
  fi
  export PATH="$PgBinDirectory:$PATH"
fi

if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "Node.js 20 or later (with npx) is required on the worker."
fi

if ! node -e 'process.exit(Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[0]) >= 20 ? 0 : 1)'; then
  fail "Node.js 20 or later is required on the worker. Found $(node --version)."
fi

# The CLI uses BACKUPDRILL_PG_DUMP / BACKUPDRILL_PG_RESTORE when the worker sets them,
# so only look on PATH when they are not set.
if [[ -z "$BACKUPDRILL_PG_DUMP" ]] && ! command -v pg_dump >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "pg_dump was not found. Install the PostgreSQL client tools (major version at least that of your Supabase Postgres) or set PostgreSQL Client Directory."
fi

if [[ "$RunDrill" == "true" ]]; then
  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "The restore drill needs a running Docker engine on the worker ('docker info' failed). Start Docker, or untick Run Restore Drill."
  fi
  if [[ -z "$BACKUPDRILL_PG_RESTORE$BACKUPDRILL_PG_DUMP" ]] && ! command -v pg_restore >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "The restore drill needs pg_restore, which was not found. Install the PostgreSQL client tools or set PostgreSQL Client Directory."
  fi
fi

# Credentials go to the CLI as environment variables, never as command-line arguments,
# because arguments are visible to every process on the worker.
export BACKUPDRILL_DATABASE_URL="$DatabaseUrl"
export BACKUPDRILL_S3_BUCKET="$S3Bucket"
export BACKUPDRILL_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$S3AccessKeyId"
export BACKUPDRILL_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$S3SecretAccessKey"
export_or_unset BACKUPDRILL_S3_ENDPOINT "$S3Endpoint"
export_or_unset BACKUPDRILL_S3_REGION "$S3Region"
export_or_unset BACKUPDRILL_PROJECT_NAME "$ProjectName"
export_or_unset BACKUPDRILL_SCHEMAS "$Schemas"

CliPackage="backupdrill@$CliVersion"
WorkDir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WorkDir"' EXIT

echo "BackupDrill - Backup Supabase Database"
echo "  Project name : ${ProjectName:-supabase}"
echo "  Schemas      : ${Schemas:-public}"
echo "  Bucket       : $S3Bucket"
echo "  Endpoint     : ${S3Endpoint:-AWS S3}"
echo "  Restore drill: $([[ "$RunDrill" == "true" ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
echo "  CLI          : $CliPackage"
echo ""

# The CLI prints progress on stderr and a JSON result on stdout. Send the progress to the
# Octopus log as normal output (Octopus shows stderr as errors) and keep the JSON for parsing.
echo "Backing up the database..."
# shellcheck disable=SC2069 # intended: stderr to the log, stdout to the file
npx --yes "$CliPackage" backup 2>&1 >"$WorkDir/backup.json"
BackupExitCode=$?
if [[ $BackupExitCode -ne 0 ]]; then
  fail "Backup failed (backupdrill exited with code $BackupExitCode). The lines above show why."
fi

# The snapshot name is the folder that holds the dump: <prefix>/<project>/<snapshot>/dump.pgcustom
SnapshotName=$(node -e '
const lines = require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").trim().split("\n");
const parts = JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]).manifest.dump.key.split("/");
process.stdout.write(parts[parts.length - 2]);
' "$WorkDir/backup.json" 2>/dev/null)

if [[ -z "$SnapshotName" ]]; then
  fail "The backup finished, but the snapshot name could not be read from the CLI output."
fi

echo ""
echo "Snapshot $SnapshotName is in bucket $S3Bucket. Restore instructions are in RECOVERY.md next to the dump."
set_octopusvariable "SnapshotName" "$SnapshotName"
StepName=$(get_octopusvariable "Octopus.Step.Name")
echo "Created output variable: ##{Octopus.Action[$StepName].Output.SnapshotName}"

if [[ "$RunDrill" != "true" ]]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Backup complete. Restore drill not requested."
  exit 0
fi

# Drill the snapshot this step just wrote rather than "latest": another deployment
# writing to the same bucket path at the same time must not change what gets verified.
echo ""
echo "Running a restore drill on snapshot $SnapshotName..."
# shellcheck disable=SC2069 # intended: stderr to the log, the JSON report is not needed
npx --yes "$CliPackage" drill --snapshot "$SnapshotName" 2>&1 >/dev/null
DrillExitCode=$?
if [[ $DrillExitCode -ne 0 ]]; then
  fail "Restore drill did not pass for snapshot $SnapshotName (backupdrill exited with code $DrillExitCode). The output above shows why. Stopping the deployment."
fi

echo ""
echo "Backup complete and restore drill passed for snapshot $SnapshotName."

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.DatabaseUrl
Parameters.Label: Database Connection String
Parameters.HelpText:
The **Session pooler** connection string of the Supabase project, from **Project Settings → Database → Connection string → Session pooler** in the Supabase dashboard. It starts with `postgresql://`. The default `postgres` user works.

Bind this to a sensitive project variable so it can be scoped per environment.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.S3Bucket
Parameters.Label: Bucket
Parameters.HelpText: Name of the S3-compatible bucket the backup is written to. It must already exist.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.S3AccessKeyId
Parameters.Label: Bucket Access Key ID
Parameters.HelpText: Access key ID with write access to the bucket. The restore drill only reads.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.S3SecretAccessKey
Parameters.Label: Bucket Secret Access Key
Parameters.HelpText: Secret access key that goes with the access key ID.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.S3Endpoint
Parameters.Label: Bucket Endpoint
Parameters.HelpText: Optional. The S3-compatible endpoint URL for Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or another provider, for example `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Leave blank for AWS S3.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.S3Region
Parameters.Label: Bucket Region
Parameters.HelpText: Optional. The bucket's region. Leave blank to use `auto`, which suits Cloudflare R2. For AWS S3, enter the bucket's region, such as `us-east-1`.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.ProjectName
Parameters.Label: Project Name
Parameters.HelpText: Optional. Name used in the bucket path (`backupdrill/<project name>/<snapshot>/`) and in the manifest. Defaults to `supabase`. Give each Supabase project that shares a bucket its own name.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.Schemas
Parameters.Label: Schemas
Parameters.HelpText: Optional. Comma-separated list of schemas to back up. Defaults to `public`.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.RunDrill
Parameters.Label: Run Restore Drill
Parameters.HelpText: After the backup, restore the new snapshot into a throwaway Postgres container and check it. If the drill does not pass, this step fails. Needs Docker and `pg_restore` on the worker, and adds the time it takes to download and restore the dump.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.PgBinDirectory
Parameters.Label: PostgreSQL Client Directory
Parameters.HelpText: Optional. A directory to put first on `PATH` so the step uses the `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` in it, for example `/usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin`. Useful when the worker has several PostgreSQL client versions installed.

Parameters.Name: BackupDrill.CliVersion
Parameters.Label: CLI Version
Parameters.HelpText: Version of the `backupdrill` npm package to run. The default `2` runs the newest 2.x release. Enter an exact version such as `2.6.0` to pin it.
